name: Florence
text: Florence (Italian: Firenze) is the capital and most populous city of the Italian region of Tuscany, and, as of 2026, with a population of 361,625, the 8th most populous city in the country. It is also the capital of the eponymous metropolitan province, which counts 988,494 inhabitants, while Eurostat estimates that 696,767 people live in the urban area of Florence. The Metropolitan Area of Florence, Prato and Pistoia, constituted in 2000 over an area of roughly 4,800 square kilometres (1,850 sq mi), is home to 1.5 million people.

depictions.text: {{Location infobox |image = Firenzelineage.png |state = Roman Republic and Empire 59 BCE–476 CEHoly Roman Empire 774–1115Republic of Florence 1115-1532Duchy of Florence 1532–1569Grand Duchy of Tuscany 1569–1801, 1815-1859French Empire 1801-1815Italy 1870–current |rulers = Republic (59-27 BCE)Autocracy (27 BCE-476)Monarchy (568-1115)Democratic oligarchic republic (1115-1532)Absolute monarchy (1532-1866) |factions = AssassinsTemplarsHouse of AuditoreHouse of Pazzi |founded = Gaius Julius Caesar |date = 59 BCE |coordinates = 43°46'23.9"N 11°15'25.1"E<ref>Assassin's Creed: Atlas</ref> |landmark = Basilica di Santa Maria del FioreBasilica di Santa Maria NovellaPonte VecchioPalazzo della Signoria }} Florence (Italian: Firenze) is a major city located in central Italy, and the capital of the region of Tuscany. During the late 15th century, the city was ruled by the powerful Medici family, and comprised four districts: Santa Maria Novella, San Giovanni, San Marco, and Oltrarno. For a brief time, the extremist Dominican friar Girolamo Savonarola ruled the city and instituted the Bonfire of the Vanities, in which thousands of items deemed sources of sin were destroyed, but a civilian uprising ended his power and the Medici were restored as the city's leaders.
